Referred to as "Mom Jo" throughout John Jackson's memoir "Please Go to Hell"; raising four sons in Depression-era Creede, she disciplined Scooter with a bar of soap over the word "crapper," grabbed her husband's revolver more than once during their arguments, and bundled up the newspaper from Saturday peanut nights for the woodstove.
Referred to as "Dad" in John Jackson's memoir "Please Go to Hell"; worked part-time as a butcher for the A. H. Major Grocery Store and taught young John arithmetic using peanuts on Saturday nights.
Father of William Thomas Jackson (1895–1957); died 1917 at Woodcroft Hospital, Pueblo, per his own death certificate (located 2026).

Referred to as "old Bullprick" in his grandson John Jackson's memoir "Please Go to Hell"; per the manuscript, committed to "Roselawn Sanitarium" and remembered by fellow miners as "crazier than hell." His own death certificate has since confirmed this was a conflation with Roselawn Cemetery, Pueblo, where he was in fact buried — the actual facility was Woodcroft Hospital, Pueblo. See his son's page for full research detail.
